purpose: Thunderpick World Championship 2026 (HLTV event 8932) days 1-3 review, the Aurora roster change, and a day-4 (17 Oct 2026) semifinal watch. Read-only: this file never creates, edits or grades a Hotspawn pick.

event.name: Thunderpick World Championship 2026
event.format_note: Two GSL groups of four, all group matches BO3; top two per group to a single-elimination BO3 playoff; third-place decider and BO5 grand final on 18 Oct.
event.playoff_note: HLTV's own playoff bracket at this read shows the semi-finals as Falcons vs BETBOOM and FURIA vs Aurora.

hotspawn_listing_status.detail: The live Hotspawn lobby tournament filter at this read lists 83 CS2 fixtures and its only Thunderpick World Championship 2026 entries are the stale 'Thunderpick World Championship 2026: South American Series #1' qualifiers (8 fixtures, June 2026). The Malta main-event day-4 semifinals are NOT on the Hotspawn board in this capture, so they are a watch item, not a pickable pick'em row.
hotspawn_listing_status.day1_day3_note: Earlier day-1 to day-3 main-event fixtures did appear on the board (for example day-1 9z vs Aurora, Hotspawn id 1080176) and their graded record is retained in hotspawn/data/pick_history.json and the archived day1/day2 research files.

days.upset_note: 9z beat Aurora 2-0 on day 1. HLTV's report describes it as a statement win against the fifth-ranked team in the VRS and credits luchov with a 1.61 rating. It is one result, not a permanent head-to-head edge: the day-3 rematch reversed it.

matches.veto: Aurora picked Cache, 9z picked Inferno; Mirage was left over. Aurora removed Nuke, the map they lost 13-1 on day 1.

matches.maps: Nuke 16-13 BETBOOM, Dust2 11-13 Legacy, Mirage 13-11 BETBOOM
matches.veto: BETBOOM removed Inferno; Legacy removed Anubis; BETBOOM picked Nuke; Legacy picked Dust2; BETBOOM removed Cache; Legacy removed Ancient; Mirage was left over.

aurora_roster_change.summary: Aurora rebuilt from an all-Turkish roster into an international one across six days in July 2026 - three players and the head coach changed. The new five debuted at BLAST Bounty 2026 Season 2 (21 July 2026), roughly three months before this event.

timeline.event: MAJ3R steps down from the active roster; soulfly is benched
Aurora sign Jimpphat (from MOUZ) and name ash (ex-GamerLegion) head coach
Aurora acquire kyxsan from Falcons as the new in-game leader, completing the rebuild

aurora_roster_change.onboarding_caution: The rebuild is dated, not fresh: the five had been together since 8 July 2026 and had already reached a top-four at this event before the day-4 semifinal. Nothing in this file converts the roster change into a numeric adjustment, and no rest or fatigue percentage is asserted.

day4.note: Not listed on the Hotspawn board at this read (see hotspawn_listing_status). Lines below are outside prices for guidance only; they are not Hotspawn picks and cannot be submitted.

market.caveat: A true 50/50 price: the market is not separating these teams. Treated as a coin flip, not an edge.

Two-way moneyline with the margin removed. bo3.gg's own page also lists Falcons to win at least one map at 1.05 and Falcons +1.5 maps at 1.05 - consistent with a strongly favoured Falcons, and a reminder that the upset case is the series, not a map.

day4.devig_method: p_a = (1/odds_a) / (1/odds_a + 1/odds_b); p_b = 1 - p_a. Decimal odds as displayed by bo3.gg for the Thunderpick market.

contrarian_read.text: With only two matches and no Hotspawn listing, the contrarian-but-not-reckless read is limited to what the market itself says. FURIA vs Aurora is priced at a coin flip, so there is no crowd favourite to fade and no edge to claim: the honest position is that this match is a toss-up. Falcons vs BETBOOM is priced about 77/23, so a BETBOOM series pick is the long-shot side of a real price rather than a random underdog - but the same page prices Falcons to take a map at 1.05, which is the market saying the upset has to be a 2-1, not a sweep. Neither statement is a probability we invented.

corrections_applied_to_shared_file.why_touched_a_file_outside_my_scope: The file publishes a start time and a probability that the pages render as fact. Both were demonstrably wrong against three timestamped machine sources in the same capture, and the start time is also the lock-deadline input. Leaving a published error in place would have broken the verify-everything rule, so the correction was made in place and logged in both files rather than duplicated into a second, contradictory source.

items.why_wrong: De-vig of 1.20 / 4.00 is (1/1.20) / (1/1.20 + 1/4.00) = 0.7692. 0.87 is neither the raw figure (0.8333) nor the de-vigged one.
items.knock_on: The same error produced a '13%' chance for BETBOOM in the upset-case prose. The true de-vigged figure is 23.1%; BETBOOM is priced at 20.5%-24.0% across the three observed sources, not 13%.
